module_dispositions.rationale: Reviewed arithmetic portability rationale; it motivates exact results but declares no independently executable operation.
Reviewed exact scaled arithmetic, rounding, remainder, and overflow operations used by numeric scanners.
Reviewed part heading and scanner recursion context.
Reviewed mandatory-brace, optional-equals, keyword, whitespace, backup, and mu-unit recovery helpers.
Reviewed internal-value forward declarations, level representation, register primitive declarations, and diagnostic spelling.
Reviewed internal dispatcher plus code-table, token-list, and identifier source families.
Reviewed mode, nest, page, shape, box, and last-item internal source families and their unavailable-state results.
Reviewed font-dimension and font-integer internal sources.
Reviewed typed register source selection and eight-bit register-index scanning.
Reviewed invalid-source recovery, level lowering, glue reference ownership, and complete-value negation.
Reviewed introduction to integer scanning and its restricted wrappers.
Reviewed every bounded integer class and its zero-valued recovery.
Reviewed optional signs/spaces, internal and character constants, radices, digit accumulation, termination, and overflow.
Reviewed introduction and result contract for dimension scanning.
Reviewed sign, shortcut/internal and numeric prefixes, point normalization, decimal fractions, and fixed-point attachment.
Reviewed infinite-order suffixes plus internal, em, ex, and mu unit selection.
Reviewed true magnification, exact physical-unit conversions, unknown-unit recovery, and max-dimen recovery.
Reviewed glue and muglue width, stretch, shrink, orders, internal fast paths, sign handling, and unit recovery.
Reviewed executable scan_toks entry, scanner-status ownership, builder initialization, collection dispatch, and result finalization.
Reviewed macro parameter and balanced-body collection, expansion/splice rules, diagnostics, and recovery.
Reviewed delimiter-code acquisition, twenty-seven-bit fallback, invalid-token backup, and null-delimiter recovery.

properties.claim: TeX82 scaled arithmetic uses fixed signed-half, decimal rounding, nx_plus_y, x_over_n, and xn_over_d rules with canonical remainders and explicit overflow signaling.
preconditions: Operands satisfy the individual routine's documented sign and range contract.
Scaled values use sixteen fractional bits and the TeX82 max_dimen bound.
stimulus: Evaluate zero, signed odd halves, decimal digit sequences through seventeen digits, exact and inexact products and quotients, and values immediately inside and outside every representable bound.
The committed command-semantic scaled-division case pins §106's x_over_n truncation toward zero for positive and negative scaled dividends.
expected_observations: Rounded scaled values, quotients, signed remainders, and arithmetic-error flags equal the numbered algorithms.
Overflow is distinguished from an ordinary negative result or nonzero remainder.
postconditions: Successful operations return exact canonical integers without floating-point dependence.
Failure leaves the caller an explicit arithmetic-error result suitable for scanner recovery.
equivalence_cases: Equivalent reduced fractions and decimal prefixes round to the same scaled value.
Positive and negative inputs follow each routine's stated sign symmetry, including odd half ties.
recovery_cases: nx_plus_y and xn_over_d overflow set the arithmetic error instead of wrapping.
Division records the canonical remainder for the caller's subsequent fraction computation.

properties.claim: Scanner syntax helpers expand through the canonical command path, skip only their specified fillers, recognize character-token syntax exactly, and restore rejected input in canonical order.
preconditions: The caller requests a mandatory left brace, optional equals, fixed lowercase keyword, or mu/non-mu compatibility check.
Current meanings, token catcodes, and scanner status are committed before lookahead.
stimulus: Present spaces, relax, macros, letter aliases, upper/lowercase character tokens, partial keywords, equals under distinct catcodes, valid braces, and rejected commands.
expected_observations: Mandatory-brace scanning skips spaces and relax; optional-equals skips spaces but not relax.
Keywords accept character tokens case-insensitively, discard only leading spaces, and reject control-sequence aliases.
A partial keyword mismatch backs up the offender and then the matched prefix as distinct input levels.
postconditions: Success consumes exactly the syntax accepted by the helper.
Missing-left-brace recovery leaves rejected input available in canonical replay order, emits the section 403 report, and accounts for the inserted brace in align_state.
equivalence_cases: Keyword letters with any character catcode and either ASCII case compare by character code.
Direct and macro-produced accepted characters share expanded-delivery behavior.
recovery_cases: A missing brace backs up the rejected command and inserts a left brace while correcting align_state.
Incompatible mu and non-mu quantities emit the canonical diagnostic and continue using the documented one-mu-equals-one-point assumption.

properties.claim: scan_something_internal dispatches code-table, token-list, token-parameter, and font-identifier commands to typed values without replaying the retained internal command.
preconditions: The current expanded command is a def_code, toks_register, assign_toks, def_family, set_font, or def_font internal command.
The caller supplies int_val or tok_val as its accepted result level.
stimulus: Fetch every code-table family and empty/nonempty token or identifier source at its legal level, then request each token/identifier source at int_val.
expected_observations: Code-table lookup scans one bounded character selector and returns its integer entry.
Token and identifier sources return typed immutable values only at tok_val, with the nested selector observation preceding the result.
postconditions: The original internal command is delivered once and the selected value preserves its source identity.
Token-list copying or formatting remains owned by the expansion consumer, not this fetch.
equivalence_cases: Direct code-table primitives and aliases with the same meaning select the same table entry.
Empty token registers and empty token parameters both return an empty typed list without fabricated tokens.
recovery_cases: A token or identifier requested below tok_val performs §416's one back_error and Missing number diagnostic inside scan_something_internal, commits dimen_val zero through §429, and leaves the caller an ordinary zero result.
An out-of-range code-table or token-register selector recovers through its restricted integer class before lookup.

cross_references.relationship: Non-owning consumer reference: §§464–472 copy or render the typed tok_val result produced here.

properties.claim: Mode, nest, page, shape, box, and last-item enquiries return the exact state-dependent TeX82 integer, dimension, or glue value without consuming operand text beyond any documented box selector.
preconditions: Mode nest, page totals, box registers, paragraph shape, and current-list tail are explicitly prepared.
The current internal command selects one enquiry family.
stimulus: Fetch spacefactor/prevdepth, deadcycles/insertpenalties, box dimensions, page totals, prevgraf, parshape size, and lastpenalty/lastkern/lastskip in every applicable and inapplicable state.
expected_observations: Each applicable enquiry returns the typed live state named by its command.
Box dimensions scan exactly one bounded register number; last-item glue retains one canonical reference.
postconditions: Read-only enquiries do not mutate the mode nest, page builder, box, shape, or current list.
The result level matches the source family before any caller-requested lowering.
equivalence_cases: Equivalent empty current lists in horizontal and vertical contexts use the documented zero last-item values.
Unset and void boxes expose zero width, height, and depth through the same box-dimension path.
recovery_cases: spacefactor outside horizontal mode and prevdepth outside vertical mode diagnose Improper and return zero.
Inactive page totals and unavailable last-item values return their canonical zero or sentinel without reading another token.

properties.claim: Font-dimension and font-integer enquiries scan the specified font and parameter selectors and return the selected metric or hyphen/skew value at its canonical level.
preconditions: Current and named fonts have explicit metric tables and integer parameters.
The current internal command selects fontdimen, hyphenchar, or skewchar.
stimulus: Read first, last, absent, and extensible font dimensions plus current and explicitly named font integer values.
expected_observations: Font identity and parameter index scans precede the typed internal result.
Existing dimensions return their exact scaled metric and integers return their assigned character code.
postconditions: A pure enquiry leaves font selection and metrics unchanged.
The result is dimen_val for fontdimen and int_val for hyphen/skew characters.
equivalence_cases: Selecting the current font explicitly or through the current-font command returns identical values.
Two fonts with equal metric entries return equal values while preserving distinct font identities during selection.
recovery_cases: A nonexistent font dimension reports the canonical error and returns zero without extending the table during a read.
An invalid font identifier recovers through the shared font-ident scanner before parameter lookup.

properties.claim: Each count, dimen, skip, and muskip internal register source scans one eight-bit index and returns the stored value at the register family's exact type level.
preconditions: Register zero, a middle register, and register 255 contain distinct typed values.
The current internal command identifies one register family.
stimulus: Fetch every register family at indexes -1, 0, a middle value, 255, and 256 using direct and expanded integer forms.
The committed command-semantic register-sources case reads §427's count, dimension, and glue register fetches back through count registers.
expected_observations: The nested integer and restricted-index results precede the internal result.
Legal indexes return integer, dimension, glue, or muglue without losing glue ownership.
postconditions: Register storage is unchanged and the result retains the selected family's type.
Exactly the selector and its canonical terminator are consumed.
equivalence_cases: Decimal, radix, character, and internal selectors denoting the same index select the same register.
All four register families share the same eight-bit selector boundary.
recovery_cases: Negative and 256 selectors diagnose their original integer and recover to register zero before fetch.
A missing selector inserts zero while preserving the rejected operand token.

properties.claim: Internal results lower only as far as the caller requests, repair glue references exactly once, negate the complete typed value when requested, and recover an invalid internal command to zero.
preconditions: A fetched source value is available at int, dimen, glue, mu, identifier, or token-list level.
The caller supplies a requested maximum level and sign.
stimulus: Request every legal lowering step and sign combination for integer, dimension, glue, and muglue values, plus a non-internal command and token/identifier below tok_val.
The committed command-semantic coercion-ownership case pins §§429–431 glue-to-dimension width selection and negation through count registers.
expected_observations: Glue lowers to its width and dimension lowers to the identical scaled integer representation until the requested level is reached.
Owned glue results retain one reference; discarded glue levels release it; negative glue negates width, stretch, and shrink without changing orders.
postconditions: The observed committed level equals the caller's requested level, not the source's original level.
No glue or token reference is leaked, duplicated, or freed while returned.
equivalence_cases: A dimension and a glue with the same width produce the same integer after complete lowering.
Negating before or after legal scalar lowering yields the same integer or dimension result.
recovery_cases: A non-internal command reports You can't use this after the and supplies zero without consuming a successor.
A token or identifier below tok_val follows §416's caller-independent Missing number recovery, single backup, dimen_val-zero commit, and §429 lowering before the scalar result observation.

properties.claim: Each restricted integer scanner first completes an ordinary integer scan, then accepts only its inclusive TeX82 range or diagnoses and replaces the result with zero.
preconditions: The exact eight-bit TeX82 profile is active.
The caller selects eight-bit, character, four-bit, fifteen-bit, or twenty-seven-bit class.
stimulus: Scan -1, 0, each maximum, and maximum plus one through direct, signed, radix, character-constant, and internal-quantity forms for every class.
expected_observations: The nested ordinary integer result is observed before restricted-class recovery.
Accepted maxima are 255, 255, 15, 32767, and 134217727 respectively.
postconditions: A legal operand is returned unchanged.
An illegal operand is returned as zero before any consuming command commits state.
equivalence_cases: Decimal, octal, hexadecimal, character, and internal forms with the same value share one bound decision.
Every consuming primitive sees the recovered value rather than applying its own clamp.
recovery_cases: Negative and above-maximum operands report the original integer in the diagnostic and recover to zero.
The following token remains available after the underlying integer scanner's canonical terminator handling.

properties.claim: scan_int expands and consumes arbitrary spaces and signs, accepts internal, alphabetic, decimal, octal, and hexadecimal constants, absorbs the specified optional space, backs up the first terminator, and saturates overflow to TeX82 infinity.
preconditions: Expanded command delivery and internal-value classification are available.
The exact-byte profile supplies TeX82 character codes and integer bounds.
stimulus: Scan empty input, multiple mixed signs, internal quantities, backtick character/control-sequence constants, every radix introducer and category variant, valid and invalid digits, category-letter/category-other A-F, lowercase terminators, boundary magnitudes, and trailing space/nonspace tokens.
The committed command-semantic integer-radix-forms case pins §§442/444 alphabetic, hexadecimal, and octal constants and a negated alphabetic constant.
expected_observations: Signs toggle negativity while spaces are ignored until the first operand.
Backtick constants consume one raw token and at most one following space.

Category-other radix introducers and digits use expanded delivery; hexadecimal A-F alone also admit category-letter tokens; the first invalid terminator is backed up unless it is the one optional space.
A completed integer observation reports the signed canonical result and radix-dependent overflow recovery.
postconditions: cur_val_level is int_val and radix records 0, 8, 10, or 16 as canonical.
Only tokens explicitly consumed by the grammar are absent from subsequent input.
equivalence_cases: Category-letter and category-other uppercase hexadecimal A-F produce equal integers; lowercase letters and recategorized decimal digits terminate the constant.
A direct character token and a one-character control sequence after backtick yield the same eight-bit code when canonically equivalent.
recovery_cases: A missing number backs up the rejected command, inserts zero, and continues without losing the offender.
A character constant above 255 reports Improper alphabetic constant and recovers to zero.
Numeric overflow diagnoses Number too big and saturates the magnitude before applying the sign.

properties.claim: scan_dimen distinguishes retained internal dimensions, shortcut integers, leading points, and ordinary integer prefixes, then attaches at most seventeen decimal digits with TeX82 rounding before sign application.
preconditions: The caller specifies ordinary or mu mode and whether an integer shortcut is already available.
Expanded delivery, scan_int, internal-value classification, and round_decimals are available.
stimulus: Scan signed whole, leading-point/comma, decimal, radix, alphabetic, internal integer, and complete internal dimension prefixes with zero, seventeen, and excess fraction digits.
The committed command-semantic dimension-fraction case pins §§452–453's leading-point fraction, a negative fraction, and an octal-prefixed dimension.
expected_observations: A leading category-other point or comma bypasses scan_int and is redelivered raw exactly once.
Only radix-ten numeric prefixes attach a fraction, and only category-other digits extend it; internal dimensions bypass numeric replay; fraction rounding feeds the exact scaled prefix.
postconditions: The prefix yields an integral/fraction pair or a complete signed internal dimension for unit processing.
The first nonfraction token remains current for the unit scanner.
equivalence_cases: Category-other point and comma with identical digits produce equal fractions; other catcodes are ordinary terminators.
Leading .5 and decimal 0.5 produce the same prefix without sharing the scan_int event sequence.
Equivalent decimal, radix, alphabetic, and internal integer whole prefixes agree before unit attachment.
recovery_cases: A missing numeric prefix follows scan_int's inserted-zero recovery while preserving the rejected token, then still performs unit recognition and optional-space scanning in canonical diagnostic order.
Fraction digits beyond seventeen are consumed but do not alter round_decimals input.
Prefix arithmetic overflow is retained for final dimension-range recovery rather than wrapping.

properties.claim: Dimension unit scanning recognizes canonical fil orders, every internal quantity as a consumed scaled unit, current-font em/ex units, and mu units with their distinct scaling, optional-space, and compatibility rules.
preconditions: A numeric integral/fraction prefix is available and the caller selects ordinary or mu units plus whether infinite units are allowed.
Current-font metrics and internal integer, dimension, glue, muglue, or §416 zero quantities are explicit.
stimulus: Attach fil through excess l suffixes, every internal level under ordinary and mu requests, em, ex, and mu to whole and fractional prefixes with case and space variants.
expected_observations: fil suffix count selects fil, fill, or filll and consumes excess l tokens after one error.
Every internal branch is consumed once and supplies its resulting value as the unit; em and ex scale both integral and fractional components, while mu is accepted only for mu dimensions.
Each accepted unit consumes exactly its documented optional following space.
postconditions: The result carries a scaled value and the normal or accepted infinite order.
Failed keyword probes retire and replay their prefixes before the next unit candidate.
equivalence_cases: Upper/lowercase keyword characters with any character catcode select the same unit.
Equivalent internal dimension, em, and ex magnitudes scale a given prefix to the same result.
Contiguous and space-separated excess l suffixes share filll recovery after documented consumption.
recovery_cases: Infinite units when inf is false fall through to ordinary-unit recovery rather than setting an order.
Excess l suffixes report one error, consume all l candidates, and clamp order to filll.
A non-mu unit in a mu scan assumes mu; mixed internal unit kinds report Incompatible glue units without an invented keyword or illegal-unit recovery.
§416's missing-number zero remains an internal unit and leaves subsequent unit-keyword text unconsumed.

properties.claim: True and physical units use TeX82's exact rational conversions and magnification adjustment, while unknown units and out-of-range magnitudes recover to assumed points and signed max_dimen.
preconditions: A finite numeric integral/fraction prefix is available in ordinary dimension mode.
Prepared magnification and exact xn_over_d arithmetic are available.
stimulus: Attach true pt and each physical unit at rounding and max-dimen edges, then use partial/unknown keywords and positive/negative overflow.
expected_observations: true divides the prefix by prepared magnification before the selected unit conversion.
Each unit uses its cited rational factor and remainder; sp skips ordinary scaling.
The final signed scaled observation follows unit parsing and optional-space consumption.
postconditions: A legal unit returns the exact platform-independent scaled value with normal order.
All failed keyword backups retire before the final result is committed.
equivalence_cases: Exact rationally equivalent values across physical units produce identical scaled results.
A true dimension at mag 1000 equals its non-true spelling; other magnifications use the documented ratio.
Upper/lowercase unit characters are equivalent while control-sequence aliases are not keywords.
recovery_cases: An unknown unit reports Illegal unit of measure, assumes pt, and replays the offender canonically.
Arithmetic or magnitude overflow reports Dimension too large, clears arithmetic error, and returns signed max_dimen.
Invalid magnification is recovered by prepare_mag before true-unit conversion.

properties.claim: scan_glue and scan_muglue accept signs, complete internal glue values or dimension widths, then independently scan optional plus and minus dimensions with canonical infinite orders and ownership.
preconditions: The caller requests glue_val or mu_val.
Scalar integer, dimension, keyword, internal-value, and glue allocation operations are available.
stimulus: Scan numeric and internal integer/dimension/glue/muglue widths with signs, absent or reordered plus/minus clauses, finite and infinite stretch/shrink, spaces, case variants, and mixed units.
expected_observations: A complete internal glue result returns without probing plus or minus and retains canonical reference ownership.
A numeric or lowered width initializes a fresh zero-glue specification before optional components.
Stretch and shrink values and orders are observed independently after their dimension scans.
postconditions: The result owns one glue specification with canonical width, stretch, shrink, and orders.
Failed optional keywords replay their partial prefixes and offender exactly as scan_keyword specifies.
equivalence_cases: Equivalent numeric and internal-integer width prefixes share the dimension-unit path.
Ordinary glue and muglue share structure while enforcing their distinct unit domains.
recovery_cases: A signed complete internal glue negates width, stretch, and shrink without changing orders.
Mixed glue kinds diagnose incompatible units and retain the requested caller level.
Malformed component dimensions recover through the dimension scanner without corrupting the allocated glue specification.

properties.claim: scan_toks installs the correct scanner status, builds canonical macro parameter and balanced replacement lists, distinguishes parameter-text numbering recovery from illegal replacement parameters, distinguishes expanded and raw collection, and splices the results of the without re-expansion.
preconditions: The caller selects macro versus general text and expanded versus unexpanded collection.
warning_index identifies the definition or absorbing owner and input delivery preserves literal brace commands.
stimulus: Collect parameterless through nine-parameter definitions, nonconsecutive and excess parameters, hash-brace forms, doubled and illegal hashes, nested groups, macros, and direct the splices in all valid mode combinations.
expected_observations: Defining or absorbing status is live for exactly the canonical collection interval and restores after completion or recovery.
Parameter text ends with end_match; body parameters become out-parameter tokens and hash-brace appends its saved brace after the body.
Unexpanded collection uses raw get_token; expanded collection expands ordinary commands one step at a time but directly copies the_toks output.
postconditions: The frozen parameter and replacement lists preserve token order, provenance, brace balance, and caller ownership.
The closing right brace is consumed by the collector and no caller token is read past completion.
equivalence_cases: Equivalent raw and expansion-stable bodies freeze identical result tokens.
Direct token-list the splices remain unexpanded whether their contents are expandable or unexpandable.
recovery_cases: Missing opening braces, nonconsecutive parameters, excess parameters, and illegal body parameters emit canonical diagnostics and insert or replay the specified token.

Nonconsecutive parameter-text numbering and illegal replacement-body parameters use distinct exact messages and help, back_error replay, inserted-token semantics, and named or active warning_index rendering.
Outer-command and EOF recovery use the live defining or absorbing status, report the partial builder, insert the canonical right brace, and continue the same sequential scan.
A right brace encountered in parameter text reports Missing left brace, terminates the definition with end_match, and returns the list built so far.

properties.claim: scan_delimiter accepts delimiter-code commands directly or scans a full twenty-seven-bit integer when required, and invalid delimiters recover to null while preserving the rejected token according to the caller's radical policy.
preconditions: The caller supplies whether a missing delimiter may be consumed for a radical.
Delimiter-code meanings and the twenty-seven-bit restricted integer scanner are available.
stimulus: Scan direct delimiter codes, numeric values from zero through 2^27 minus one, negative and overflowing integers, and tokens with no delimiter meaning under radical and non-radical policies.
expected_observations: Direct delimiter codes are used without an integer scan.
Numeric fallback observes the ordinary integer and restricted result before constructing small and large family/character fields.
An invalid non-radical token is backed up with its traced origin.
postconditions: A valid operand fills all delimiter fields from the canonical twenty-seven-bit layout.
Recovery returns the null delimiter and leaves subsequent input positioned by the caller policy.
equivalence_cases: A direct delimiter meaning and an integer encoding with identical fields produce the same delimiter.
All legal high-bit combinations through the full twenty-seven-bit maximum are preserved.
recovery_cases: An invalid delimiter reports Missing delimiter, inserts a period conceptually, and yields null fields.
Non-radical scanning backs up the rejected token; radical scanning consumes it.
Out-of-range numeric operands recover through scan_twenty_seven_bit_int to zero.
